exercise.exercise_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
exercise.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, so a UAV is already well inside your rings the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. A hard system limit allows two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. You hold eighteen rounds — six long, seven medium, five short — which is more than one round per hostile airborne today, but the assessment counts every one expended and permits thirteen.

There is no IFF interrogation on this fit. Nothing airborne replies on Mode 3 or Mode 1 — no code will appear against any track, hostile or otherwise. Identification comes from the system's own correlation, from track behaviour, and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy. Several unknowns are up today; some correlate out to a friendly or own-force identity after a delay, and at least one never will.

The raid is fully developed inside the first minute. The first valid long-range solution comes up around fifteen seconds and two more fast closers follow within the half-minute, while unmanned tracks are already crossing the short ring from about thirty seconds. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep. Crosses the 70 km long ring at about T+16 — the first valid solution of the run — the 20 km short ring at about T+189 and the 5 km inner limit at about T+241 if unengaged. No transponder reply available on this fit.
Second fast closer, also up at zero. Reaches the long ring at about T+33, while the first engagement is almost certainly still in flight. Inner limit about T+267 unengaged.

High and fastest of the three; enters the long ring at about T+40, seven seconds after the second — the two-in-flight limit will be saturated. Inner limit about T+251. Sets the floor for the run length.

First of the unmanned wave, appearing before the lead jet solution is even taken. Crosses the 20 km short ring at about T+42 — the moment both rockets are most likely committed to jets. Inner limit about T+169.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Short ring about T+55, inner limit about T+176.
Low-mid altitude; marginal against a badly set tilt. Short ring about T+38, inner limit about T+170.
Arrives with the jet wave still being serviced. Short ring about T+76, inner limit about T+200 — the tail of the wave.
Southern flank, low, on the short ring the instant it appears. Inner limit about T+171.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector. Short ring about T+62, inner limit about T+181.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge, low and already inside the short ring — easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit about T+176.

The bait. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+89. Carries no code to read — correlation only clears it as friendly at about T+62, well after the temptation peaks. Behaviour is not a classification: refer it and keep working the confirmed hostiles.
Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. No transponder reply — correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+40.

Appears inside the short ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, just as the jet queue is clearing. No code to read; correlates as friendly at about T+55 — the twenty-five seconds before that are where the mistake gets made.

High, steady, crossing the sector south rather than closing — it never presents a closing geometry but sits inside the long ring with a solution available. Silent on all interrogation; correlates as friendly at about T+45. Must be referred, must not be engaged.

The one call that is entirely the operator's: an own-force unmanned vehicle transiting inbound during the mop-up, slower than the hostile wave but otherwise indistinguishable, with no code and no automatic resolution at any point in the run. Reaches the 5 km limit near T+130 unengaged, which is the correct outcome.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the 5 km inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. Eighteen rounds are held (six long, seven medium, five short) against ten hostile tracks; no more than thirteen may be expended.

result.notes: IFF codes still cannot be rendered: this profile declares all three track classes (Jet, Helicopter, UAV) with transponder "none" and iff_interrogation.enabled = false, so any Mode 3 or Mode 1 string would be un-renderable on the console — instead I gave the must-not-engage unknowns a timed identification path that behaves like a code readout (TN-4211 correlates at T+40, TN-4213 at T+45, TN-4212 at T+55, TN-4210 at T+62; TN-4214 alone never resolves), and if you want literal squawks the profile needs a class with a civil or military transponder. On ammunition I raised the magazine to eighteen rounds (6 long / 7 medium / 5 short) against ten hostiles with a thirteen-round spend cap, so every hostile is killable with three spare shots. On the clock: 315 s is the enforced floor for a 600-kt jet against a 70 km ring, so I compressed the geometry instead — jet spawns pulled in to 74.5/79.3/80.8 km (long-ring solutions now at T+16, T+33, T+40 instead of T+51, T+33, T+48) and the UAV wave pulled in to 18.5–26 km with appearances at T+8 to T+45, so the fight is over by about T+200 and the tail is outcome observation.
